Then, about two months ago, something shifted. I stopped sleeping—like, I didn’t *want* to. My body just wouldn’t sit still. I paced my apartment, rubbed my hands together, couldn’t keep still even when exhausted. I’d talk and talk, words spilling out—my coworkers kept saying, “Whoa, slow down.” I didn’t mean to snap at people, but little things—someone’s tone, a delayed med order—would set me off. I bought so much online—clothes, tech, things I didn’t need—maxed out my card. 

And sometimes… I feel things. Like bugs crawling under my skin, but there’s nothing there. Or I’ll hear people in the ER exchange a glance and just *know* they’re talking about me, sending me messages. 

But I can’t tell if this is one long spiral or two separate storms—one crashing into the other.

For two months straight, I barely slept—maybe two hours a night—and I was wired, pacing the locker room between shifts, my hands never still, rubbing my arms like something was crawling under my skin. I’d talk so fast the doctors couldn’t get a word in during handoffs, and I snapped at anyone who tried to slow me down. I maxed out three credit cards buying clothes and medical gadgets I didn’t need, telling myself I was starting a clinic. I even thought security guards were sending coded messages to me through their radio static—like it was all about my “mission.”  

Then, just as suddenly, that energy crashed. For the past five months, I can’t feel anything. Not joy, not love, not even worry. I stand in front of the fridge for twenty minutes just trying to decide what to eat. I called in late to shifts, forgot meds—I’m not safe right now. But those voices, those skin-crawling sensations? They only happened when I was manic. They’re gone now.

Messages in interviews, glances in crowds. I hear her voice sometimes, whispering encouragement when I’m editing late. Not like a memory—she’s *speaking*, clear as you are now.

I shot three short documentaries back-to-back without rest, talking constantly on set, barely letting anyone get a word in. My crew said I was intense—snapping at small delays, calling people lazy if they questioned my ideas.  

About six weeks in, I became convinced that a famous journalist I’ve never met—someone I admire—was sending me secret signals through her interviews. I believed she was in love with me, that we were meant to work together. I started leaving her long voice messages, even flew to where she was filming once. I could *hear* her voice sometimes, not like an echo—clear, direct, telling me I was destined to change the industry.  

But none of this felt out of place at the time. It all made perfect sense—until last week, when the energy just crashed. That’s when I realized how out of control it got. The voices are gone now, and I’m embarrassed by what I did. But during those two months, the mania and the voices—they were all happening together. I wasn’t hearing voices before or after. Just during that time.
D010-D005_h006.question_b:

For two solid months, I was unstoppable—sleeping maybe two hours a night, talking so fast my crew couldn’t keep up, pouring money into a film project no one thought was viable. I maxed out credit cards, convinced it was a genius move, that investors were just too shortsighted. I was irritable—snapping at people for tiny mistakes, pacing constantly.

But here’s what’s not normal: even after that frenzy burned out, the voices stayed. I hear a woman’s voice, clear as you talking to me, telling me she’s in love with me, that she’s sending me signs through the TV. I know it sounds strange, but she’s real to me. She’s not part of any “high” or energy spike—that phase is gone. But the voice? Still here every day. And it’s been like this for six months now, long after I calmed down. I can’t focus, can’t pitch new projects, my ex says I’m not the man I was. The psychosis didn’t fade when the mania did. It just… stayed.

D010-D005_h019.question_both:
I’ve been up here at the station for over eight months now—just me, the light, and the sea. It started slow… I can’t remember the last time I felt joy. Nothing feels real, nothing feels worth doing. I lie in bed most nights, staring at the ceiling, waiting to fall asleep—sometimes takes hours, if it happens at all. I keep thinking, “Maybe tomorrow I won’t wake up,” not because I want to end it, but because it'd just be easier.

Then, about three weeks ago, something shifted. I didn’t need sleep. My mind raced—thoughts tumbling over each other, like waves crashing. I cleaned the whole tower twice in one night, repainted the railing bare-handed, paced for hours in the howling wind. I snapped at the supply boat guy for no reason—he just asked if I was okay. My words came so fast even I couldn’t keep up.

And… I can’t explain this, but I started feeling things. Like something’s crawling under my skin, especially at night. Doesn’t stop. Even now, I feel fingers brushing my arm—nothing’s there. I’m terrified. The world feels wrong, like it’s fading out. Like none of this will matter soon—like it’s all going dark.
D010-D005_h019.question_a:
I’ve been the keeper here at the lighthouse for twelve years now—just me, the waves, and the fog. For about seven months, I couldn’t get out of bed most days. Everything felt hollow. No joy in anything, not even watching the sunrise over the water like I used to. I’d lie there, wide awake at night, heart racing, thinking, “What’s the point? I wish I wouldn’t wake up.” But I never planned anything—just… tired of existing.

Then, three weeks ago, something flipped. I went from not sleeping to not needing sleep. I was rewiring the entire beacon system in the middle of the night, pacing, my mind racing faster than I could speak—my words tumbled out so fast I could see the relief officer mouthing “slow down.” I snapped at him over nothing—just a clipboard misplaced. And I started to feel… poisoned. Not literally, but like dark tendrils were crawling under my skin, slithering up my arms. I could *feel* them—no bugs, no rash, but I scratched until I bled. I became certain the lighthouse was the last standing structure after the world ended—like a beacon over nothing. 

But here’s the thing—those feelings, the crawling, the certainty about the end—they only started when I got this manic energy. Never before, never in the dark months. As soon as the energy started fading, the visions did too.
D010-D005_h019.question_b:
I’ve been the keeper at this lighthouse for twelve years now, and things have… changed. About seven months ago, I stopped feeling anything—just empty. I couldn’t sleep at first, lying in the dark for hours, listening to the waves, thinking, “What’s the point of any of this? The world’s already over. Nobody sees the light anymore.” I stopped going to the mainland even for supplies.

Then, three weeks ago, something switched. I was suddenly awake all the time—like my blood was buzzing. I paced the tower for hours, couldn’t sit still, talking fast to the radio even when no one answered. I was sure I had to warn someone—something huge was coming, a wave that would swallow everything. I felt it crawling on my skin, like something was moving under my clothes, but when I looked… nothing.

Now, the energy’s gone, but the thoughts haven’t. The darkness is still here. I still feel that creeping sensation. But the rage, the speed—it’s mostly passed. I see it now: that wild three weeks was just a burst in the middle of this long, slow collapse. The voices and the crawling… they never left, even when I’m not “manic.” They’re just… part of the silence.

But then, about three weeks ago, something shifted. I didn’t need sleep. I felt sharp—like I could work 36 hours straight and still ace every decision. I was talking fast, ideas spilling out, people kept asking me to slow down. I barely sat down—I was charting, calling consults, pacing the halls. I started thinking I could… I don’t know, revolutionize patient care. Like I was meant for something huge, beyond residency. And sometimes, late at night, I’d feel something crawling on my arms—like bugs—but when I looked, nothing was there.

Now I’m crashing again. But were those weeks real? Or was I sick then? I can’t tell where one state ends and the other begins.
